n: The Lord introduces himself as Alpha and Omega and as the crucified Redeemer, speaking to the troubled Colesville Saints in Thompson, Ohio.
Newel Knight, the branch leader, is told to stand firm in his calling despite the turmoil.

f.g: Leader of the Colesville Saints; his healing from an evil influence in 1830 was among the Church’s first recorded miracles.

n: If the Saints want to escape their enemies, they must repent fully and become humble and contrite.

f.g: Sorrowful for sin, humble, and teachable.

n: The consecration covenant at Thompson has been broken—Leman Copley withdrew the land he had promised—so the agreement is now void.
Woe to the one responsible for this offense; it would have been better for him to drown in the sea. Jesus used similar words about those who cause others to stumble.

f.w: drowned in the depth of the sea

n: Those who kept the covenant and the commandment are blessed and will receive mercy.
So they must leave Thompson before their enemies come, choose a leader, and appoint someone to handle their money.

f.g: An old phrase meaning “come now” or “go ahead.”

n: They are to travel west to Missouri, to the border with the Native American lands.

f.g: The western edge of Missouri, beyond which lay Indian Territory.

n: Once there, they should earn a living like anyone else until the Lord prepares a place. Faith does not replace work.

f.w: seek ye a living like unto men

n: Be patient in trials until the Lord comes. He comes quickly, bringing reward, and those who sought him early will find rest for their souls.
